topic: Principle of operation of powered control (electro hydraulic servo motors)
syllabus_extract: Principle of operation of powered control (electro hydraulic servo motors).
specific_objectives: 14.2.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain the functions of AFCS.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Demonstration of Servo Motor operation using PPT schematics; Safety: Do not touch live electrical components; Supervision: Instructor monitors trainee observation.
intro_questions: What is the primary function of the AFCS?
How does a manual control system differ from a powered control system?
What is the role of the servo motor in the flight control system?

topics: Components of Electro Hydraulic Servo Motor
Signal flow from pilot input to actuator
Feedback loop mechanism in servo motors
development.content:
Definition and purpose of AFCS
Components of Electro Hydraulic Servo Motor
Signal flow from pilot input to actuator
Hydraulic power supply requirements
Feedback loop mechanism in servo motors

Operation during normal flight conditions
Response to pilot command inputs
Automatic trim and stabilization functions
Failure modes and system redundancy
Interaction with flight control computers

Maintenance checks for servo motors
Troubleshooting common hydraulic leaks
Electrical fault diagnosis procedures
Testing servo response times
Record keeping for AFCS inspections

summary_questions: Explain the sequence of events when a pilot inputs a control command.
Describe how the feedback loop ensures accurate servo motor positioning.
Identify two potential failure modes in an electro hydraulic servo system.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on how the principles of servo motors discussed in this lesson apply to the automatic trim control system covered in LP 02.
